judged_text: The diff adds an ungated Salesforce token refresh (fetch + statusText check + credential write) that runs on every SalesforceCalendarService construction, where previously jsforce refreshed lazily only when the stored access token was rejected. Every Salesforce booking/availability check on every install (no feature flag, contrary to the PR's opt-in sync objective) now pays a login.salesforce.com round-trip plus a DB write, and a Salesforce outage or transient network failure fails operations that previously succeeded with the valid stored token; the response.statusText !== "OK" check also throws HttpError 400 behind proxies that strip HTTP reason phrases.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the diff adds an unconditional refresh-token exchange against `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` plus a `prisma.credential.update(...)` before returning the `jsforce.Connection` (i.e., executed whenever this code path runs), with no gating on `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` or `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`. This is a behavioral regression vs. a lazy/only-on-failure refresh strategy: it introduces a network dependency and DB write into the normal path and can fail operations during transient Salesforce/network issues even if the stored token remains valid. Additionally, the error check `if (response.statusText !== "OK")` is brittle (reason phrases may be empty/modified by proxies); `response.ok`/`response.status` should be used, so this can incorrectly throw `HttpError(400)` despite a non-error response semantics.
